dataset.name: WattPair Appliance Load & Surge Provenance Dataset
dataset.description: Running watts, start-up surge, duty cycle and annual energy for 30 household and off-grid appliance classes, where every figure carries the source document it was read from, the tier of that source, the date it was verified and a confidence rating. The distinguishing property is not coverage but provenance: fields we have found no published figure for are present and explicitly null rather than filled with an estimate, and the basis of each surge figure is labelled (nameplate locked-rotor amperage, manufacturer-stated, category envelope, or unknown) so a reader can tell a measured inrush from a rule of thumb. Compiled from manufacturer specification sheets and manuals, government efficiency filings and standards documents. Published by WattPair under CC BY 4.0.

dataset.method: Compiled with AI assistance from manufacturer documents, government efficiency filings and standards bodies, then checked against the cited source. Every non-null figure carries the URL it was read from, so any claim here can be re-derived from public documents without trusting this file.
dataset.coverage_note: This dataset is deliberately incomplete and says where. For several appliance classes we have found no published start-up surge figure; those fields are null with a status of unknown rather than estimated, and the site makes no claim that the figure exists nowhere. Where a null field carries an absence_verified block, that block names the documents that were read and the date they were read on. Read stats.null_fields, stats.absence_verified_fields and stats.surge_basis before using any figure.

pending_fields.test_conditions: Per-field test conditions (what was measured, under what load, at what voltage). Recorded for every non-null figure, in Chinese. English translation is stage P-A.
pending_fields.source_label: Human-readable label for each source document. The machine-readable source_url, source_type and source_tier are exported now.
pending_fields.short_description: One-paragraph description of each appliance class.
pending_fields.blocking_reasons: Why a record is not yet cleared for page generation. The boolean ready_for_page_generation is exported now, and so is the count of reasons.

dataset.out_of_scope: Power-station records, solar-panel records, the compatibility engine and every commercial mapping are deliberately not part of this dataset.

constants.note: Two engine constant tables, without which the appliance records are not self-explanatory: a surge duration in milliseconds cannot be used correctly unless you know which band it falls in, and a missing power factor cannot be filled in without the default table. Both are derived from public standards and manufacturer documents.

absence_verified.note: A band needs two ends from the same market, and this record has one figure per market rather than a spread within either. The pair that stood here until 2026-08-08 was a US machine at the low end and a UK machine at the high end — the same cross-market shape removed from washing-machine on the same day, and a spread across two mains standards is not a spread across a category. Within the US market we hold two Hamilton Beach rating tables, and both give the same number: doc 840228502 covers models 40864/40865/40866/40869/40876 at 120 V~ 60 Hz 1500 W, and Hamilton Beach's own product pages restate 1500 W for the 1.7-litre 40869 and the 1-litre 41065. Two readings of 1500 W are one point, not a range, so no US band is published here. The per-market figures live at the top level (US) and in region_profiles.EU. This record's load type is resistive, so the engine never read these two keys as a modulation curve; what they drove was the range printed on the page.

Same reading as the low end. The 3000 W that stood here until 2026-08-08 is the Russell Hobbs Buckingham 20460, a 230 V UK kettle, and it was the top of a range shown on a US-first page whose other end was a 120 V machine. It now lives only in region_profiles.EU.running_watts, where only EU stations meet it. One sourced EU model is one point, and we did not go looking for a second one to manufacture a European band out of; the record says what it holds.

The manufacturer's German user manual (2,296 lines of extracted text, including the complete Technische Daten table) was searched in full for Anlaufstrom, Einschaltstrom, Startstrom, Anlauf, blockierter Rotor, locked rotor and LRA: all seven terms return zero hits. The manual's only electrical entries are the EN 60335-1 nameplate rating and the rated figures for the two operating modes — no transient quantity of any kind. The EU EPREL registration (2517927) was pulled in full and confirms that Regulation 626/2011 asks split units for no start-up current, and in fact for no rated input power or rated current either. For a variable-speed compressor this absence is structural.

A watt band needs a second and a third machine whose real power is published, and on 2026-08-08 the electrical tables of every sump-pump document this record cites were read column by column for one. Liberty Pumps prints MODEL / HP / VOLTAGE / PHASE / FULL LOAD AMPS / LOCKED ROTOR AMPS / OVERLOAD TEMP / WINDING CLASS on both the 250 and the 280 engineering sheets and no watt column. Zoeller's FM2778 MODEL COMPARISON prints HP, voltage, phase, amps, RPM, motor type and insulation class and no watt column. Little Giant is the one maker in the class whose table carries a WATTS column, and it carries a single figure (720 W) for every 6-CIA item number, so it supplies a point and not a band. The current spread across the class is therefore recorded where it is measurable — as apparent power, in `apparent_power_va` (598–1116 VA) — and this field stays empty rather than restating volt-amps under a watt label, which is the exact defect G-42 was opened to remove.

Same reading as the low end of the band. The machine that would set the top of a watt band is the Zoeller M53, whose current draw (9.7 A at 115 V) is the highest in the class, and neither the dealer-hosted FM2778 copy nor the manufacturer's own current revision 0724 of that sheet carries a watt figure for it — the MODEL COMPARISON table stops at amps. Its apparent power is held in `apparent_power_va.value_max` (1116 VA) with its source intact.

On 2026-08-08 three Zoeller documents were opened and searched for a duty cycle, a cycles-per-hour count or a minutes-per-hour figure. Zoeller technical data sheet FM2778 (the whole MODEL COMPARISON and PRODUCT SPECIFICATIONS tables) prints HP, voltage, phase, amps, RPM, motor type, insulation class and motor protection, and no duty cycle. Installation and operating manual FM2676 prints none either; its only statement on the subject is that the installer should obtain the proper tether to customize the on-off cycle to each application — the manufacturer saying the on-off rhythm is set on site. Zoeller's own article What Is the Optimum Sump Pump Run Time? opens by stating that there is no set optimum run time for a sump pump; what it does give is installation guidance (avoid short cycling, target a minimum of one minute per cycle with at least five minutes of rest between activations, and note that fifteen to twenty cycles per hour could overheat the pump), which is an install-time setup target and not the measured duty cycle of any model. No duty cycle is derived from that guidance: the actual value is set by groundwater infiltration rate, a property of the site rather than of the machine, so this is a structural absence and not a gap a further search would close. The unblocking path is user input (pit depth, infiltration rate, on-off interval).

This record's load type is inverter_driven_motor, and for that type the engine reads running_watts_low and running_watts_high as the bottom and the top of ONE machine's power-modulation curve, not as a spread across models (engine/compat.ts documents the distinction on the field itself). No such curve is published for any washing machine this record cites. LG's WM4000HWA specification sheet states a POWER SOURCE line — 120V, 10 Amps — and no minimum or maximum power input; GE's GFW350SSYWW sheet states an Electric Rating of 120V 11.0A 60Hz and likewise no power range; Bosch's WAN28281GB manual states a single Nominal power of 2300 W plus per-programme energy per cycle, which is energy over a whole cycle and not the instantaneous floor and ceiling of a modulating drive. The pair of figures that stood here until 2026-08-08 was a US machine at one end and a European machine at the other, which is neither one machine nor one market; it is now removed rather than restated, and the per-market figures live in region_profiles. What a modulation curve would unblock is a runtime interval instead of a point; the verdict itself is unaffected, because with no range the engine judges on the region-resolved running_watts.

Same reading as the low end. The 2300 W that stood here until 2026-08-08 is the Bosch WAN28281GB's nominal power on a 220-240 V supply — a European machine that heats its own water — and it was being applied as the top of the modulation curve for US pairings as well, so a 120 V verdict was decided by a machine not sold in the United States. Bosch publishes one nominal power and no modulation range; the figure now lives in region_profiles.EU.running_watts, where only EU stations meet it.

Regulation (EU) 2019/2014 declares no annual figure for washing machines at all — the label and the registry carry energy consumption per 100 cycles. A published EPREL washing-machine record was pulled in full on 2026-08-03 to confirm the field set rather than assume it (registration 1145659, Bosch WIW28443, used here only as a probe of the schema): it exposes energyConsPer100Cycle = 62 and no annual-consumption field of any kind. Turning 100-cycle energy into an annual figure would take a cycles-per-year assumption that no EU document supplies, so this field stays empty rather than carrying an invented one.

Three official Midea U-series user manuals (5,306 lines of extracted text between them) were searched in full for LRA, locked rotor, inrush, starting current, rated current, amps, amperes, watts and rated power: all nine terms return zero hits in all three documents. These manuals carry no electrical specification table at all — not even a running current. The ENERGY STAR certified room air conditioner dataset (446 units, 28 fields) has no start-up current or locked-rotor field: the field does not exist rather than being left empty. For a variable-speed compressor this absence is structural, not a gap in our searching.

On 2026-08-08 the three Midea U-shaped inverter window-AC manuals this record already cites were re-read in full and word-searched for duty cycle, modulation, part-load and compressor speed. The only hit is one operating instruction in the MAW08U1QWT manual (in TurboCool the unit runs at the highest fan and compressor speed); no modulation curve and no time fraction appear anywhere. The DOE test procedure at 10 CFR 430 subpart B appendix F and the ENERGY STAR certified room-AC dataset were checked the same day. Appendix F does publish three numbers for variable-speed room air conditioners, and none of them is a duty cycle: (1) the weighting factors Wtc across the four condenser-inlet test conditions (95/92/87/83 °F, 0.08 for the first) weight outdoor-temperature bins for an efficiency rating, not run time; (2) the cycling loss factor CLF describes the theoretical comparable SINGLE-speed unit the variable-speed machine is scored against, not the variable-speed machine itself; (3) the 0.75 coefficient in AECcool is, in the regulation's own words, 750 annual operating hours multiplied by a 0.001 kWh/Wh conversion — an annual-usage assumption, a different quantity from the fraction of rated power this field would carry, and mistaking one for the other would present annual energy as an instantaneous load. No usable figure exists in any of these sources.
